title: TEMPO config
description: One schema for both TEMPO config files: a repo's .tempo/config.yaml and a workspace's .tempo/workspace.yaml. A file with a 'workspace' key is a workspace file.

template.description: Text with placeholders in single braces, filled at run time: {ticket} {slug} {branch} {nn} {type} {scope} {summary} {pattern} {module} ({task} is an old alias of {ticket}). A local T-NNN task id is never filled into a template. ${env:NAME}, ${workspace} and ${repo} are filled when the config is resolved.

command.description: Shell command run from the repo or worktree root. null means not available.

env.description: Environment variables set for every command, worktree setup step and agent shell.

test_one.description: Runs one test or pattern. Use {pattern}, and {module} for multi-module builds.

test_local.description: The local tier's test-one command, with the same placeholders as test_one, pointed at a runner that skips what only CI runs (widget or browser tests, for example). Under gates.full_bars: ci, `cmd test_one` prints it. null: test_one.

branch.description: The task branch. It is the integration branch and the PR branch, the only branch TEMPO pushes, so it follows the repo's convention. {type} is the change's Conventional Commits type (feat, fix, chore ...), mapped through branch_types. SHALL NOT start with tempo/. Default: {type}/{ticket}.

branch_types.description: The word the repo's branches use for each Conventional Commits type, filled into {type} in git.branch. Example: {feat: feature, fix: bugfix}. Types not listed use their own name. When neither this nor git.branch is set, TEMPO reads the words from the remote branches.

work_order_branch.description: One per Work Order. Local only, never pushed. SHALL NOT be '{branch}/...': git cannot hold a branch and a branch below it. {name} is the task branch without its first path segment (feat/AV-1 gives AV-1); {branch} is the whole task branch. Default: tempo/{name}-wo-{nn}.

repro_branch.description: Bug flow reproduction branch. Local only, never pushed. Default: tempo/{branch}-repro.

worktree_root.description: Relative to the repo root unless absolute.

delete_merged_local_branches.description: After SHIP, delete local work-order and repro branches whose work the task branch holds (merged, same patches, or folded before the PR). Branches with unshipped commits, pushed or checked-out branches and the task branch are kept. Never touches remote branches.

language.description: BCP 47 tag for commit messages, for example en or pt-BR.

extra_args.description: Appended to every git commit, for example --no-verify.

fold_fixes.description: Before the PR is pushed, fix commits are made as fixup! commits of the commit they correct and squashed into it before SHIP, so the PR shows one commit per feature step. Commits after the PR is open are never rewritten.

tool.description: none: TEMPO pushes nothing and prints the commands.

language.description: BCP 47 tag for the PR title and body.

body_template.description: Path to a markdown file used as the PR body layout, relative to the repo root. Default: .github/pull_request_template.md when present.

required_checks.description: Checks CI-WAIT waits for before it reads a round (limits.ci_rounds above 0): until one reports it counts as pending. Name the ones that appear late, such as a commit status posted when its run ends (ai-review). No shell characters or parentheses: the spawn guard allows the watcher only with plain arguments, so require a gate check such as ci-gate rather than a matrix job named 'flutter (core)'.

worktree.description: How to make a new worktree usable. A worktree has only tracked files.

copy.description: Gitignored files or folders copied from the main checkout, relative to the repo root (.env files, local secrets, generated config).

link.description: Gitignored folders symlinked instead of copied (large caches such as node_modules). Ignore them without a trailing slash: `node_modules/` matches a folder, not the symlink a worktree gets. Builders never stage these paths, and setup excludes them in info/exclude.

setup.description: Commands run in order inside the new worktree after copy and link. {worktree} is the worktree's name as a safe identifier, for a per-task database such as app_{worktree}.

teardown.description: Commands run inside a worktree before SHIP removes it, for what setup created. {worktree} as in setup.

before_run.description: Commands tempo_run.py runs at the root of a task worktree before each command, never in the main checkout: clears what one run leaves that breaks the next (generated plugin sources, a stray Podfile). A failing step is named in the summary and does not stop the run.

full_bars.description: When TEMPO runs the full suite. on_demand: Integrate runs NARROW bars; the full suite runs for critical changes and on /tempo:verify. integrate: every task's final integrate runs it. verify: never inside a task, critical or not; bars prints a DEFERRED line, targets print scoped runs only, and the full suite runs on the branch the task merges into or on /tempo:verify. ci: the light local tier for a repo whose PR checks run the suites: every integrate runs only the touched tests and their mirrors (test_local when set), one typecheck of the touched packages and lint; no whole package, no build, no platform target; bars prints BARS: LOCAL and DEFERRED: ci. Pair it with limits.ci_rounds, so the task waits for those checks.

full_paths.description: Globs. A change to a matching file runs FULL bars even when full_bars is on_demand.

tests.description: Test files that need their own handling, as repo-relative paths. bars --paths prints them as ALWAYS: and SLOW: lines.

always.description: Files the integrator runs at every NARROW integrate, from their own package, whatever packages the change touches (a guard test that must never be skipped).

slow.description: Files too slow to run whole on every change. Builders and QA run them filtered to the groups a change touches; the integrate after the last wave runs each one the change touches or mirrors whole, once.

review_extensions.description: Extra review rounds Jorge may grant at LOOP-LIMIT. After them, new findings ship as known risks.

narrow_fix_lines.description: A fix round whose changed lines stay at or under this count gets a narrow review. 0 turns narrow rounds off.

split_orders.description: HANDOFF splits a single-repo task into stacked slices when it would issue more Work Orders than this. 0 turns splitting off.

split_criteria.description: HANDOFF also splits when the Spec has more acceptance criteria than this. 0 turns this trigger off.

spec_slice_kb.description: Above this Spec size in KB, each Work Order carries the Spec terms and design bullets it needs, so the builder does not read the whole Spec. 0 turns it off.

ci_rounds.description: Above 0, the task waits on the PR after SHIP (stage CI-WAIT): it fixes red checks and blocking review findings in plain commits, at most this many rounds, and ends only when the PR is merged. TEMPO never merges. 0 (default): the task ends when the PR opens.

order_check.description: After each Work Order builds, a quick reviewer checks that order's diff (correctness, edge inputs, its rules) and its builder fixes what it finds before the order integrates. M and L lanes.

id.description: ticket: the task ID is the ticket key found in the request (falls back to sequence). sequence: T-001, T-002 ... A T-NNN id is local to one checkout and never leaves .tempo/.

ticket_pattern.description: Regex for ticket keys, for example [A-Z]+-\d+. With a capture group, the group is the key: (?:#|/issues/)(\d+) for GitHub issues.

trackers.description: Every tracker this project takes tickets from. The ticket that appears first in the request picks its tracker and becomes the task ID. Replaces tracker and ticket_pattern.

ticket_pattern.description: Regex for this tracker's keys. With a capture group, the group is the key: (?:#|/issues/)(\d+) for GitHub issues.

sync.description: Opt-in: TEMPO assigns and moves the ticket. Absent: TEMPO never writes to it.

assign.description: Assign the ticket to you when the task starts building.

start.description: Status (Jira: transition or target status name) when the task starts building.

pr.description: Status when the task's PR opens.

merged.description: Status when CI-WAIT sees the PR merged (limits.ci_rounds above 0). Leave it out when the repo's CI moves the ticket on merge.

project.description: GitHub only: owner/number of the Projects board whose Status field moves, e.g. my-org/4.

standing_decisions.description: Decisions Jorge has already made for this project, one per line (for example a delivery order or a scoping rule). Triage and the orchestrator apply them instead of raising GATE-CLARIFY, and record which one they applied.

autopilot.description: Run every task as if --auto were given: TEMPO accepts its own recommendation at each gate and escalation, logs it in decisions.md, and stops only for the questions orchestrator §4.5 keeps. --no-auto on a command turns it off for that task.

qa.description: How QA brings up the product and shows each acceptance criterion working in it: API calls, the web app in a browser, the mobile app on an emulator or simulator, with evidence saved under .tempo/<task>/qa/.

live.description: true (default): QA checks every criterion in the running product. false only for a repo with nothing to run (a library).

surfaces.description: What QA starts, in start order. A list replaces the inherited one as a whole.

kind.description: service: started for others (a db, an emulator), never checked itself.

start.description: Started with <procs> start; {worktree} is filled as in worktree.setup.

ready.description: Regex in the start output that means it is up (<procs> start --ready).

url.description: Base URL QA calls or opens, e.g. http://localhost:3000.

health.description: Exits 0 when the surface answers, e.g. curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health.

screenshot.description: Writes a screenshot to {out}, e.g. adb exec-out screencap -p > {out}.

needs.description: Surfaces listed earlier that must be up first.

paths.description: Globs or re: regexes; the surface applies when a changed file matches. None: always.

accounts.description: Sign-ins QA uses. Real values go in config.local.yaml or ${env:NAME}, never in config.yaml.

seed.description: Creates the data and accounts QA needs; run once after the surfaces are up.

toolchain.description: Name of a toolchain in the workspace file.

path.description: Repo root, relative to the workspace root.

depends_on.description: Repos whose change this repo builds on. Sets the order of per-repo tasks.

toolchain.description: Name of a toolchain in the workspace file.
Name of a toolchain in the workspace file.

defaults.description: Settings every repo in the workspace starts from.

validation.description: How a workspace task checks its repos together locally (JOINT-QA).

steps.description: Commands run in order from the workspace root, e.g. starting the local stack.

teardown.description: Commands that stop what the steps started.

docs.description: Docs shared by every repo of the workspace, relative to the workspace root.

Where the project's own documentation lives. Agents read it before searching the code. Paths are relative to the file's root: the workspace root in a workspace file's top-level docs, the repo root in a repo entry or a repo's config.yaml.

paths.description: Each entry is a folder (every doc file under it), a glob (`docs/**/*.md`, `**/ADR-*.md`), or a regex over the root-relative path prefixed with `re:` (`re:^services/[^/]+/docs/.*\\.md$`).

exclude.description: Globs or `re:` regexes removed from the matches.

index.description: File names treated as index files and listed first. Default: index.md, README.md.

rules.description: true (default): docs that state conventions, ADRs or a design system count as rules for the spec lens and the spec pre-check.

targets.description: Extra test runs for platforms the main test command does not cover (a web build, a device). The architect adds a target to a Work Order's verification when the order changes a file under its paths; the integrator runs every target the diff touches, scoped to the tests the diff touches when scoped_command is set.

command.description: Run from the repo or worktree root, for example: cd flutter-client && melos exec -- flutter test --platform chrome.

paths.description: Globs relative to the repo root. The target applies when a changed file matches one.

scoped_command.description: The same run limited to some test files, used whenever the changed files map to tests. {package} is the package directory relative to the repo root ('.' for the root), {tests} the test files relative to it. Example: cd {package} && flutter test --platform chrome {tests}. Without it the full command runs.

run.description: routine: runs at every integrate, scoped. final: runs once, scoped, at the integrate after the last wave (targets --final). critical: runs only for critical changes and on /tempo:verify. ci: never on this machine, /tempo:verify included; the PR's CI runs it. Default: critical for an advisory target, routine otherwise.

advisory.description: true: the target is known to fail on the base branch. Its failures are compared with the base's and reported, and only failures the base does not have block. Set it while the base is red; remove it once the base is green.

test_globs.description: Globs for the test files a runner runs, matched against the path or the file name, for scoped runs. Default: *_test.*, *.test.*, *.spec.*, test_*.py, *Test.java, *Test.kt. Other changed files in test folders (helpers, fixtures) are listed as NO-TESTS.

package_markers.description: File names that mark a package root, for scoped runs ({package}). Default: pubspec.yaml, package.json, go.mod, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts).
